title: Judges Chapter 18 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Judges chapter 18 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Judges Chapter 18 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Judges Chapter 18.

questions.question: In Judges 18, what was the reason the tribe of Dan sought an inheritance to dwell in?
options: Because all their inheritance had not fallen unto them among the tribes of Israel
Because they wanted to expand their territory
Because they were commanded by a prophet
Because they were driven out by enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Because all their inheritance had not fallen unto them among the tribes of Israel
questions.explanation: Judges 18:1 states that the tribe of Dan sought an inheritance because unto that day all their inheritance had not fallen unto them among the tribes of Israel.

questions.question: How many men did the children of Dan send to spy out the land?
questions.correctAnswer: Five
questions.explanation: Judges 18:2 says the children of Dan sent five men from their coasts to spy out the land.

questions.question: From which two places did the five men sent by the Danites come?
questions.correctAnswer: Zorah and Eshtaol
questions.explanation: Judges 18:2 identifies Zorah and Eshtaol as the coasts from where the five men came.

questions.question: True or False: The five men who came to the house of Micah knew the voice of the young Levite.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 18:3 clearly states that the five men knew the voice of the young Levite when they were by the house of Micah.

questions.question: What role did the Levite say he had with Micah?
questions.correctAnswer: He was his priest
questions.explanation: Judges 18:4 states that the Levite said Micah had hired him and that he was his priest.

questions.question: What did the five men ask the Levite to do for them?
options: Ask counsel of God about their journey
questions.correctAnswer: Ask counsel of God about their journey
questions.explanation: Judges 18:5 records that the men asked the Levite to ask counsel of God so they might know if their way would be prosperous.

questions.question: True or False: The priest told the men that their way was not before the LORD and they should turn back.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 18:6 states the priest said, 'Go in peace: before the LORD is your way wherein ye go,' indicating their way was indeed before the LORD.

questions.question: When the five men arrived at Laish, how did they describe the people living there?
questions.correctAnswer: Careless, quiet, and secure
questions.explanation: Judges 18:7 describes the people of Laish as dwelling careless, quiet, and secure, with no magistrate in the land.

questions.question: What did the five men say to their brethren when they returned to Zorah and Eshtaol?
options: The land is barren and dangerous
They should arise and possess the land because it is very good
They should wait for more men
They should make peace with Laish
questions.correctAnswer: They should arise and possess the land because it is very good
questions.explanation: Judges 18:9 records the five men urging their brethren to arise and go, for the land they saw was very good.

questions.question: True or False: The men described the land of Laish as lacking many resources and difficult to possess.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 18:10 states the land had no want of anything and God had given it into their hands, meaning it was rich and easy to possess.

questions.question: How many men did the tribe of Dan send out to possess the land?
questions.explanation: Judges 18:11 states that six hundred men appointed with weapons of war went from Zorah and Eshtaol.

questions.question: Where did the six hundred men of Dan first pitch their camp after leaving their homes?
questions.correctAnswer: Kirjathjearim in Judah
questions.explanation: Judges 18:12 says they pitched in Kirjathjearim, in Judah, and called it Mahanehdan.

questions.question: Which comes first in Judges 18: the five men spying the land or the six hundred men going up to possess it?
options: The six hundred men going up to possess the land
The five men spying the land
questions.correctAnswer: The five men spying the land
questions.explanation: Judges 18:2 shows the five men went first to spy out the land, and Judges 18:11 shows that after their report, six hundred men went up to possess it.

questions.question: True or False: The tribe of Dan had already received all their promised land inheritance before this chapter.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 18:1 states that the tribe of Dan sought an inheritance because all their inheritance had not yet fallen unto them.

questions.question: What did the five men do when they came to the house of Micah?
options: They ignored the house and went on
They sent a message from afar
questions.correctAnswer: They lodged there
questions.explanation: Judges 18:2 says the five men came to the house of Micah and lodged there.

medium.title: Judges Chapter 18 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Judges Chapter 18 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What was the name given to the place where the Danites pitched their camp in Judah?
questions.correctAnswer: Mahanehdan
questions.explanation: Judges 18:12 states that the Danites pitched in Kirjathjearim but called that place Mahanehdan. This shows their identification with their tribe while in Judah.

questions.question: When the Danites came to Mount Ephraim, whose house did they visit?
questions.correctAnswer: Micah's
questions.explanation: Judges 18:13 says they came to the house of Micah in Mount Ephraim, a key location for the narrative that follows.

questions.question: What items did the five men who spied out Laish report were in Micah's house?
options: An ephod, teraphim, a graven image, and a molten image
Only an ephod and a graven image
A bronze altar and sacred vessels
questions.correctAnswer: An ephod, teraphim, a graven image, and a molten image
questions.explanation: Judges 18:14 lists these specific items found in Micah's house, indicating religious objects significant for their plans.

questions.question: How many men armed for war did the Danites mobilize to go against Laish?
questions.explanation: Judges 18:16 and 18:11 indicate that 600 men were appointed with weapons of war, ready for the mission.

questions.question: Where did the 600 men stand while the five men entered Micah’s house?
options: At the entering of the gate
At the city gates of Laish
questions.correctAnswer: At the entering of the gate
questions.explanation: Judges 18:16 specifically says the 600 men stood at the gate's entrance while the five men went inside.

questions.question: What was the priest's initial reaction when the five men took the religious items from Micah's house?
questions.correctAnswer: He asked, 'What do ye?'
questions.explanation: Judges 18:18 records the priest's question, showing his surprise and confusion about the theft.

questions.question: What argument did the Danites use to persuade the priest to join them?
options: Being priest for a tribe is better than for one man
They said he would be king
questions.correctAnswer: Being priest for a tribe is better than for one man
questions.explanation: Judges 18:19 records their reasoning, appealing to his desire for greater influence and honor.

questions.question: What was the priest's emotional response to the Danites' proposal?
questions.correctAnswer: His heart was glad
questions.explanation: Judges 18:20 says the priest's heart was glad, indicating his eagerness to join the tribe.

questions.question: What did the Danites place before them as they departed from Micah’s house?
questions.correctAnswer: Little ones, cattle, and carriage
questions.explanation: Judges 18:21 describes them putting children, livestock, and carriages at the front, showing a full migration.

questions.question: What happened when the men near Micah’s house overtook the children of Dan after they had departed?
questions.correctAnswer: They cried out to them
questions.explanation: Judges 18:23 shows that the men called out to the Danites, seeking to understand their actions.

questions.question: How did Micah respond when confronted about the loss of his gods and priest?
options: He questioned what more he had
questions.correctAnswer: He questioned what more he had
questions.explanation: Judges 18:24 records Micah’s response, expressing despair at losing his gods and priest.

questions.question: What advice did the Danites give Micah to protect his life?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 18:25 shows the Danites warning Micah not to raise his voice lest he lose his life, indicating their threat.

questions.question: Did Micah attempt to fight the Danites after realizing they were too strong?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 18:26 states that Micah turned back to his house when he saw the Danites were too strong, showing he did not fight.

questions.question: The Danites destroyed the city of Laish and built a new city called Dan in its place.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 18:27-29 describe how the Danites smote Laish with the sword, burnt the city, then rebuilt it and named it Dan after their ancestor.

questions.question: How does Judges 18 teach about the importance of trusting God’s guidance when making significant decisions?
options: By showing the Danites asked the Levite priest for counsel about their journey’s success
By illustrating Micah’s peaceful acceptance of losing his gods
By emphasizing the Danites’ military strength alone
By highlighting the priest’s initial refusal to join the Danites
questions.correctAnswer: By showing the Danites asked the Levite priest for counsel about their journey’s success
questions.explanation: Judges 18:5-6 illustrate the Danites seeking God’s guidance through the priest, teaching reliance on divine counsel before action.

hard.title: Judges Chapter 18 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Judges Chapter 18.

questions.question: What did the children of Dan say to Micah when he confronted them for taking his gods and priest?
options: Let not thy voice be heard among us, lest angry fellows run upon thee
We will return what we took and make peace with you
We acted under God's command to take possession of the land
We will give you another priest in your place
questions.correctAnswer: Let not thy voice be heard among us, lest angry fellows run upon thee
questions.explanation: Judges 18:25 shows the children of Dan warning Micah to keep silent so he would not be harmed by angry men.

questions.question: What happened to the city of Laish according to Judges 18?
options: It was smitten with the sword and burnt with fire
It was made a tributary to the Danites
It was spared after a peaceful negotiation
It became a religious center for Israel
questions.correctAnswer: It was smitten with the sword and burnt with fire
questions.explanation: Judges 18:27 states the Danites attacked Laish, killing its inhabitants and burning the city.

questions.question: Why was there no deliverer for the people of Laish?
options: Because it was far from Zidon and had no business with any man
Because they were protected by a strong king
Because they were allied with the Danites
Because they had fortified walls and many soldiers
questions.correctAnswer: Because it was far from Zidon and had no business with any man
questions.explanation: Judges 18:28 explains Laish had no deliverer due to its remote location and lack of allies.

questions.question: What new name did the children of Dan give to Laish after capturing it?
questions.correctAnswer: Dan
questions.explanation: According to Judges 18:29, the city formerly called Laish was renamed Dan after the tribe's ancestor.

questions.question: Who was Jonathan in relation to the priests serving the tribe of Dan?
options: Son of Gershom, son of Manasseh, serving as priest
A warrior who led the Danites
questions.correctAnswer: Son of Gershom, son of Manasseh, serving as priest
questions.explanation: Judges 18:30 identifies Jonathan as the son of Gershom and a priest to the Danites.

questions.question: What did the children of Dan set up in their new city that Micah had made?
questions.correctAnswer: A graven image
questions.explanation: Judges 18:31 states the Danites set up Micah's graven image in their city.

questions.question: What literary device is exemplified by the repeated mention of Micah’s graven image before and after the Danites’ actions?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: The chapter begins and ends by referencing Micah's graven image, framing the narrative and demonstrating inclusio.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word "ephod" mentioned in Judges 18:14 primarily refer to?
options: A priestly garment or sacred vestment
questions.correctAnswer: A priestly garment or sacred vestment
questions.explanation: The ephod was a sacred priestly garment used in Israelite worship, as seen in Judges 18:14 and in other priestly contexts.

questions.question: According to Judges 18:26, what was Micah’s response after finding himself too weak to confront the Danites?
options: He turned and went back unto his house
He gathered more men to fight
He appealed to the elders of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: He turned and went back unto his house
questions.explanation: Judges 18:26 records that Micah retreated to his house after realizing he was overpowered.

questions.question: Which verse indicates that the Danites initially sent five men to spy out the land before moving to take possession?
questions.correctAnswer: Judges 18:2
questions.explanation: Judges 18:2 describes the sending of five valiant men to spy out the land for the Danites.

questions.question: True or False: The Danites acted to possess the land of Laish because God had given it into their hands according to their spies' report.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 18:10 states the spies assured the people that God had given the land into their hands, encouraging them to possess it.

questions.question: True or False: The Danites returned Micah’s gods and priest after taking the city of Laish.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 18:27–31 shows the Danites took Micah’s gods and priest with them and set up the graven image in their new city.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage shares a thematic connection with Judges 18 regarding the unauthorized use of priestly objects and images?
options: 1 Samuel 4, where the Ark of the Covenant is captured
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Samuel 4, where the Ark of the Covenant is captured
questions.explanation: The unauthorized handling of sacred objects in Judges 18 parallels the capture of the Ark in 1 Samuel 4, showing tensions over holy items.

questions.question: How does the phrase 'In those days there was no king in Israel' (Judges 18:1) relate to the situation described in this chapter?
options: It highlights the lawlessness and tribal autonomy leading to the Danites' actions
It signifies the peaceful unity among tribes
It indicates the presence of a strong centralized government
It refers to the time of King David
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights the lawlessness and tribal autonomy leading to the Danites' actions
questions.explanation: Judges 18:1 sets the context of decentralization and disorder, which allowed the Danites to act independently without a king.

questions.question: What does the interaction between the Danite spies and the young Levite indicate about religious leadership in Israel at that time?
options: Religious leadership was decentralized and often hired by individuals
The Levites had centralized authority over all Israel
The Danites were rejecting Levite leadership
Only priests from Shiloh were legitimate
questions.correctAnswer: Religious leadership was decentralized and often hired by individuals
questions.explanation: Judges 18:4 shows the Levite was hired by Micah, showing religious roles were localized and not centralized.

theological.title: Judges Chapter 18 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Judges Chapter 18 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What theological condition does Judges 18:1 reveal about Israel during the time of the Danites seeking an inheritance?
options: Israel was united under a strong king
There was no king in Israel, indicating a period of decentralized leadership
Israel had conquered all their promised land
The tribes were all settled peacefully
questions.correctAnswer: There was no king in Israel, indicating a period of decentralized leadership
questions.explanation: Judges 18:1 states 'In those days there was no king in Israel,' revealing a theological condition of Israel's lack of centralized human leadership, which led to tribal unrest and spiritual instability.

questions.question: According to Judges 18:6, what divine attribute is demonstrated when the Levite priest gives counsel to the Danite spies?
options: God’s omniscience in knowing all things
God’s providential guidance and peace to His people
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providential guidance and peace to His people
questions.explanation: In Judges 18:6, the priest says, 'Go in peace: before the LORD is your way wherein ye go,' showing God's providence and peace as He directs His people’s path.

questions.question: What doctrinal implication does Judges 18:10 teach regarding God's sovereignty over the land?
options: The land is given by human conquest alone
God has given the land into the hands of the Danites, showing divine sovereignty over territorial possession
The land is cursed and inhospitable
The land belongs to the Zidonians
questions.correctAnswer: God has given the land into the hands of the Danites, showing divine sovereignty over territorial possession
questions.explanation: Judges 18:10 states 'for God hath given it into your hands,' teaching the doctrine that God sovereignly grants possession of land to His people, a theme consistent with divine providence (see also Deuteronomy 8:7-10).

questions.question: How does Judges 18:14 reveal theological concerns about idolatry within the tribe of Dan?
options: It praises the spiritual devotion of Micah's house
It reveals the presence of an ephod, teraphim, and graven image, indicating syncretism and idolatry within Israel
It forbids the use of any religious images
It shows that the tribe of Dan worshiped only the true God
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals the presence of an ephod, teraphim, and graven image, indicating syncretism and idolatry within Israel
questions.explanation: Judges 18:14 lists multiple idolatrous objects 'an ephod, and teraphim, and a graven image,' showing the syncretistic worship practices that contradict the exclusive worship of Yahweh.

questions.question: What does Judges 18:19 suggest about the priest’s motivation in joining the Danites, and what doctrine might this expose regarding human sinfulness?
options: He seeks to serve God faithfully
He desires greater honor and influence, reflecting human ambition and self-interest
He wants to return to Micah’s house
He is forced against his will
questions.correctAnswer: He desires greater honor and influence, reflecting human ambition and self-interest
questions.explanation: The priest’s willingness to leave Micah and serve a tribe reveals human sinfulness, including ambition and desire for status, rather than faithfulness to true worship (Judges 18:19).

questions.question: How does Judges 18:27 contribute to the theological narrative of Israel’s conquest and the judgment of nations?
options: It shows peaceful coexistence with Laish
It shows the Danites smiting Laish and burning their city, reflecting divine judgment through Israel’s conquest
It shows Laish conquering the Danites
It records a covenant between Dan and Laish
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the Danites smiting Laish and burning their city, reflecting divine judgment through Israel’s conquest
questions.explanation: Judges 18:27 narrates the destruction of Laish by Dan, which fits into the biblical theme of God using Israel to execute judgment on other nations (cf. Joshua 6).

questions.question: What does Judges 18:29 teach about the significance of naming places in the biblical narrative?
options: Names are given randomly without meaning
Naming the city Dan after the tribe’s ancestor highlights the importance of tribal identity and covenantal heritage
The city was named after a Canaanite god
questions.correctAnswer: Naming the city Dan after the tribe’s ancestor highlights the importance of tribal identity and covenantal heritage
questions.explanation: Judges 18:29 shows the city named Dan after the tribe’s patriarch, emphasizing continuity of covenantal promises and identity (cf. Genesis 49:16-17).

questions.question: Considering Judges 18:30-31, what theological problem is illustrated by the establishment of idolatrous worship in Dan?
options: Faithful worship of Yahweh was preserved
The tribe of Dan perpetuated idolatry by maintaining Micah’s graven image and unauthorized priesthood, violating covenantal commands
The people worshiped only in Shiloh
questions.correctAnswer: The tribe of Dan perpetuated idolatry by maintaining Micah’s graven image and unauthorized priesthood, violating covenantal commands
questions.explanation: Verses 30-31 reveal that Dan set up Micah’s idol and had priests not from the authorized Levitical line, showing apostasy and disobedience (cf. Deuteronomy 12:13-14).

questions.question: What synthesis doctrinal insight can be drawn by combining Judges 18:1 and Judges 18:31 regarding leadership and idolatry in Israel?
options: The absence of a king led to spiritual chaos and idolatry in Israel
The Levites always led Israel faithfully
questions.correctAnswer: The absence of a king led to spiritual chaos and idolatry in Israel
questions.explanation: Judges 18:1 states there was no king in Israel, and 18:31 shows idolatry flourishing, illustrating how lack of godly leadership resulted in spiritual disorder, a theme echoed in 1 Samuel 8.

questions.question: What combined teaching about divine guidance and human disobedience emerges from Judges 18:6 and Judges 18:27?
options: God’s guidance always leads to obedience and holiness
Despite God’s providential guidance ('Go in peace'), human agents still act violently and sinfully, as seen in the conquest and destruction of Laish
Human actions are independent of divine will
questions.correctAnswer: Despite God’s providential guidance ('Go in peace'), human agents still act violently and sinfully, as seen in the conquest and destruction of Laish
questions.explanation: Judges 18:6 shows God’s peace and direction, but 18:27 reveals that human responses include violent conquest and idolatry, highlighting the tension between divine providence and human sinfulness.

questions.question: What does the narrative of Judges 18:14-19 combined teach about the dangers of religious syncretism and unauthorized priesthood?
options: Religious syncretism and unauthorized priesthood lead to spiritual corruption and departure from true worship
Idolatry is permitted if led by priests
The Levite priest was faithful to God
questions.correctAnswer: Religious syncretism and unauthorized priesthood lead to spiritual corruption and departure from true worship
questions.explanation: Verses 14-19 show the Danites appropriating idols and a Levite priest for their own use, illustrating the theological error and spiritual corruption caused by mixing true worship with idolatry and unauthorized religious leadership.

questions.question: From Judges 18:9-11, what theological principle about human responsibility and divine promise can be inferred?
options: Humans must be passive and wait for God to act
God’s promises require human courage and action to possess what He has given
God’s promises are unconditional regardless of human response
Possession of land is due to human strength alone
questions.correctAnswer: God’s promises require human courage and action to possess what He has given
questions.explanation: In verses 9-11, the Danites are urged to arise and possess the land God has given, teaching that divine promises involve human responsibility to act in faith.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted by Judges 18:28 regarding the security of Laish before its conquest?
options: God’s justice in allowing judgment on complacency
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice in allowing judgment on complacency
questions.explanation: Judges 18:28 describes Laish as 'quiet and secure' but later destroyed, illustrating God's justice in judging complacent nations who do not seek Him (cf. Psalm 73:18-20).

questions.question: How does Judges 18:12 contribute to understanding the Danites’ strategy in their migration and settlement?
options: They first pitched near Judah in Kirjathjearim, naming it Mahanehdan, indicating a temporary staging area before full conquest
questions.correctAnswer: They first pitched near Judah in Kirjathjearim, naming it Mahanehdan, indicating a temporary staging area before full conquest
questions.explanation: Verse 12 shows the Danites camping at Kirjathjearim, naming it Mahanehdan, revealing an organized approach to securing territory stepwise.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that divine guidance is inconsistent because the Levite priest in Judges 18 leads the Danites into idolatry. What does Judges 18:6 and 18:19-20 actually teach about God's guidance and human responsibility?
options: God directs all human actions, including sin
God provides guidance and peace, but humans retain responsibility and can misuse that guidance for sinful ends
questions.correctAnswer: God provides guidance and peace, but humans retain responsibility and can misuse that guidance for sinful ends
questions.explanation: Judges 18:6 shows God’s peace and direction, yet verses 19-20 reveal the Levite’s complicity in sin, teaching that divine guidance does not override human free will and accountability (cf. Deuteronomy 30:19).
